name: Julia Letlow

issue_poll.name: Combined: Pelican Institute Q1 2026 Pelican Pulse, Louisiana voters, Feb 20-24, 2026; Emerson College/KLFY Louisiana GOP primary poll, Apr 24-26, 2026; LSU Reilly Center 2025 Louisiana Survey, Feb-Apr 2025
issue_poll.note: No fall 2026 Louisiana poll with a full issue ranking was found (the Oct 2026 Hart and Jul 2026 PPP Davis-campaign polls reported only the horse race). Top two come from the Pelican Pulse Feb 2026 statewide poll (cost of living/inflation 40%, economy 18%); its full table (Excel) could not be fetched. Ranks 3-10 ordered by the full LSU 2025 Louisiana Survey table (average of online and phone: crime 13.5%, education 12.5%, budget/taxes/spending 7.5%, infrastructure 7%, insurance 4%, health care 4%, coast/environment/weather 3.5%; https://msg.lsu.edu/reillycenter/research/louisiana-survey/la_survey_pdfs/2025_la_survey_report.pdf), adjusted by Emerson's Apr 2026 poll (Republican primary voters only: economy 43%, crime 16%, education 10%, health care 9%, immigration 8%; https://emersoncollegepolling.com/louisiana-2026-poll-fleming-letlow-cassidy-in-close-three-way-race-for-senate/), which moved health care and immigration up. LSU's 'other social issues (abortion, guns)' bucket (4.5%) was left out because it bundles two separate issues.

issues.detail: Make no-tax-on-tips and no-tax-on-overtime permanent; expand Child Tax Credit; increase domestic energy production
Expand oil, gas and Gulf offshore production; speed LNG export approvals; protect Jones Act; expand domestic shipbuilding
Raise fentanyl trafficking penalties; designate Mexican drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations
Pass national Parents' Bill of Rights (parental notice, curriculum transparency, records access); expand school choice
Implement MAHA agenda: food labeling transparency, stricter nutrition standards in federal programs, prevention focus; no vaccine mandates
Codify DOGE spending cuts; extend Trump tax cuts permanently; oppose tax increases; shrink federal bureaucracy
Strengthen levees; expand navigation channel dredging; modernize ports and inland waterways; expand rural broadband
Finish border wall; nationwide E-Verify mandate; cut sanctuary city funding; end catch-and-release; exclude illegal immigrants from census
Reform National Flood Insurance Program; roll back FEMA premium increases; risk-model transparency; more mitigation funding
Protect and expand GOMESA revenue sharing; accelerate coastal restoration; reform FEMA to speed disaster payments

plan_caveats: Could not confirm the Nov 3, 2026 general-election result from a source; winner status (CBS News projection) taken from the task.
No fall 2026 Louisiana issue ranking found; ranking combines a Feb 2026 statewide poll (top two only), an Apr 2026 Republican-primary-only poll, and the 2025 LSU survey.

Nearly all ratings rest on the campaign's 15-point 'Julia's Plan' page, which lists items with no numbers, dates or bill numbers; Concrete ratings rely on clear end states (permanence, codification, named Parents' Bill of Rights, E-Verify mandate, border wall completion).

Taxes: the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill already made most 2017 tax cuts permanent, so that item partly points to existing law; Concrete rating rests on codifying DOGE cuts. 'Oppose tax increases' comes from an OnTheIssues summary of an Apr 2026 pledge that could not be confirmed at the source.
Cartel terrorist designation was already done by executive action in 2025; crime rated Partial since no checkable new measure is stated beyond higher fentanyl penalties of unspecified size.

Health care plan is mostly food and nutrition (MAHA); 'lower healthcare and prescription drug costs' is stated with no measure. Vaccine-mandate stance is from a campaign interview (https://www.aol.com/articles/exclusive-julia-letlow-discusses-trump-015207882.html).
Letlow declined the October 2026 general-election debate and did not answer the WWNO/WRKF candidate questionnaire; her campaign-site 'theissues' page is an old House-race page and was not used.
Her March 2026 House bill (Judicial Efficiency and Reform Act) and other House votes were excluded as past record.
